territory.label: Anti-Hype
territory.lens: strip the marketing away — mud, sweat and plain talk
territory.description: The brand that refuses launch theater: no ads, no gloss, no influencer seeding — let unedited runners and raw results carry the story.

big_idea: The Unlaunch: the brand ships with zero advertising — no campaign, no influencers, no launch film. It appears only as plain-text race results, unedited shoe-repair logs, and a homepage that is a live spreadsheet of everything the company spent and emitted that month.

art_direction.imagery_direction: Deliberately unproduced imagery: runners' own phone photos, mud-caked shoes on doormats, screenshot-quality plainness; the only designed object is the spreadsheet itself.
art_direction.layout_notes: Default-looking on purpose: system-font look, visible table borders, underlined links; resist all decoration except one warm accent.

copy.headline: We spent the ad budget on the shoe.
copy.subhead: No campaign. No launch film. A spreadsheet, a shoe, and whatever runners say about it.
copy.body: Every marketing dollar is a dollar that didn't go into the midsole, so we cut the category's biggest emission first: the hype. Our homepage is the company ledger, our campaign photography is whatever your phone shot at mile nine, and our launch event is a race we didn't sponsor.
taglines: Marketing is the first emission we cut.

critique.case_against: Anti-marketing is itself a well-worn marketing trope, so the pose reads as knowing rather than honest, and a seed-stage brand with zero paid reach has no mechanism to be discovered at all — an unlaunch by an unknown is indistinguishable from silence. The spreadsheet homepage entertains insiders but taxes conversion for everyone else, and the concept says almost nothing about the shoe itself: it is a media strategy wearing a brand strategy's clothes, and it collapses the moment the company runs its first promotion.
